Rowe Price]] (23%) | industry = [[Investment management]] | products = {{ubl|[[Asset Management]]|[[Wealth Management]]}} | aum = {{increase}} {{INRConvert|1689318|C}} {{small|(July 2024)}}{{cite web|url=https://www.livemint.com/market/stock-market-news/uti-amc-q2fy24-earnings-net-profit-drops-9-to-rs-183-crore-aum-up-1689-11697628491427.html|title=UTI AMC Q2FY24 earnings: Net profit drops 9% to ₹183 crore; AUM up 16.89%|website=www.livemint.com|date=16 July 2024}} | area_served = India and 35 other countries | num_employees = 1,422 (2026) | website = {{URL|https://www.utimf.com}} }} '''UTI Asset Management Company''' ('''UTI AMC''') is an Indian [[List of asset management firms|asset management company]]. It manages mutual funds, portfolio management services, and retirement solutions for individual and institutional investors. UTI Mutual Fund was launched by the [[Government of India]] in 1963, and it is one of the oldest [[Asset management|mutual fund companies]] in India. == History == The Unit Trust of India (UTI), first mutual fund in India, was set up by an Act of [[Parliament of India|Parliament]] in 1963. Mutual funds in India are constituted in the form of trusts under the Indian Trusts Act of 1882. The Unit Trust of India aimed to encourage saving by providing for various classes of investors the facility of investing their money in units of the Trust. In 1964, UTI launched its first investment scheme Unit Scheme-1964 initially RBI had the regulatory and administrative control. UTI had the monopoly of the mutual fund industry till 1987 when the [[Government of India]] permitted public sector banks and financial institutions to sponsor mutual funds.{{Cite web |title=The Unit Trust Of India Act, 1963 |url=https://indiankanoon.org/doc/179933/ |website=indiankanoon.org}}{{Citation |chapter=7 The Unit Trust of India and the Indian Mutual Fund Industry |title=India at the Crossroads -- Sustaining Growth and Reducing Poverty |date=15 February 2001 |chapter-url=https://www.elibrary.imf.org/display/book/9781557759924/ch007.xml |access-date=2024-07-16 |publisher=International Monetary Fund |language=en |isbn=978-1-55775-992-4}} [[File:Stamp of India - 2014 - Colnect 505730 - Unit Trust of India UTI.jpeg|left|thumb|Golden Jubilee Year - Commemorative Stamp]] Under Unit Scheme-1964, UTI had sold and repurchased the units at prices fixed arbitrarily by its management rather than on the basis of the actual value of the underlying assets, attributing to its abnormally high dividends. Investment decisions based on political compulsions taken by those in key positions exacerbated by the political instability in the 1990s and the consequent market rout and took a toll on the Unit Scheme-1964 which ultimately led to the government intervention in 2002 with a bailout package and the act to repeal and transfer the undertakings of the trust.{{Cite web |date=2001-08-13 |title=UTI crisis: Political parties use and abuse India's largest mutual fund |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/magazine/cover-story/story/20010813-uti-crisis-political-parties-use-and-abuse-indias-largest-mutual-fund-774002-2001-08-12 |access-date=2024-07-16 |website=India Today |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2001-07-23 |title=UTI flagship scheme US-64 pauperised by former chairman by gambling on high-risk shares |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/magazine/economy/story/20010723-uti-flagship-scheme-us-64-pauperised-by-former-chairman-by-gambling-on-high-risk-shares-773882-2001-07-22 |access-date=2024-07-16 |website=India Today |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2021-12-27 |title=Backstory: The US-64 crisis and how the government bailed out UTI investors - CNBC TV18 |url=https://www.cnbctv18.com/market/backstory-the-us-64-crisis-and-how-the-government-bailed-out-uti-investors-11939132.htm |access-date=2024-07-16 |website=CNBCTV18 |language=en}} Erstwhile Unit Trust of India was bifurcated with the non-NAV based schemes brought under the government purview and other under the purview of SEBI. While the former came under the Administrator of the Specified Undertaking of The Unit Trust of India (SUTTI) and the latter became the asset manager, UTI Mutual Fund.{{Cite news |date=2002-10-29 |title=Govt breaks the Trust, finally scraps UTI Act |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/economy/policy/govt-breaks-the-trust-finally-scraps-uti-act/articleshow/26556467.cms |access-date=2024-07-16 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}}{{Cite web |title=Administrator of the Specified Undertaking of The Unit Trust of India |url=http://www.suuti.in/DOCS_PDF/About_SUUTI_October_2022.pdf |website=www.suuti.in |access-date=16 July 2024 |archive-date=3 July 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240703235619/http://suuti.in/DOCS_PDF/About_SUUTI_October_2022.pdf |url-status=dead }}{{Cite web |first= |title=THE UNIT TRUST OF INDIA (TRANSFER OF UNDERTAKING AND REPEAL) ACT, 2002 |url=https://lddashboard.legislative.gov.in/sites/default/files/A2002-58.pdf |website=legislative.gov.in}} == Specified Undertaking of UTI == Restructuring of Unit Scheme-1964 brought the large equity holdings along with other assets including real estate and 25 assured-return schemes to the Specified Undertaking of The Unit Trust of India (SUTTI). As of 2016, SUTTI had stakes in 43 listed and 8 unlisted companies valued more than Rs. 60,000 Crores.{{Cite news |title=Government starts process for sale of SUUTI Holdings |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/economy/finance/government-starts-process-for-sale-of-suuti-holdings/articleshow/53124225.cms |newspaper=The Economic Times|date=9 July 2016 }} == UTI Mutual Fund == Considering the active schemes, UTI Mutual Fund is one of the oldest mutual fund companies in India. UTI Mutual Fund has been a pioneer in launching various schemes, such as the UTI Unit Linked Insurance Plan (ULIP) with life and accident cover (launched in 1971), UTI Master Share (launched in 1986), India's first Offshore Fund – India Fund (launched in 1986), and the UTI Wealth Builder Fund, the first of its kind in the Indian mutual fund industry combining different asset classes like equity and gold, which are lowly correlated. The company manages the portfolios of domestic and offshore funds and offers discretionary, non-discretionary and advisory services to HNI clients, corporates, and institutions; and also offers retirement solutions and private equity funds in India and 35+ countries through the principal and subsidiary business entities. It also manages [[pension fund]]s in India and currently has an investor base of more than 12 million live folios. UTI Mutual Fund has a nationwide reach through its distribution channels. It currently operates more than 190 branches across the country. As of 2024, UTI AMC has an Assets Under Management (AUM) of Rs.15.56 lakh crores. == See also == * [[Mutual funds in India]] * [[Government of India]] ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== *[https://www.utimf.com Official Website] *[https://utifunds.com.sg/ International Website] *[https://www.amfiindia.com/research-information/mf-history History of Mutual Funds in India] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180618175239/https://www.amfiindia.com/research-information/mf-history |date=18 June 2018 }} {{Major asset management companies}} {{authority control}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Unit Trust Of India}} [[Category:Mutual funds of India]] [[Category:Government-owned companies of India]] [[Category:Financial services companies based in Mumbai]] [[Category:Financial services companies established in 1963]] [[Category:1963 establishments in Maharashtra]] [[Category:Companies listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange]] [[Category:Companies listed on the National Stock Exchange of India]] [[Category:Asset management companies]]
